text:
maria: seeing memory climb steadily during a long streaming chat + tool-loop run in staging, hit ~72GB. KV resident never drops between tool calls. paging counters spike every ~15s. repro attached. anyone seen this pattern?

ajay: can you paste the --kv-stats output or runtime profiler snapshot? also which commit / canary?

maria: repro on canary (deploy id: d-2026-0315-09). kv-stats snippet:
```
kv_pages_total=2145
kv_pages_active=1876
kv_page_reuse_rate=0.12
kv_pager_reads=14321
kv_pager_writes=512
pager_evictions=340
kv_slot_frag_pct=38
```

maria: pager_reads jumps in lockstep with tool loop cadence. looks like we keep faulting pages back in instead of reusing. :thinking_face:

chris: pprof of allocator during repro shows hot path in copy-on-read when page miss happens. also see extra pinned buffers from the kernel path chosen for quantized attention matrices.

leo: note: we recently adjusted the batching heuristics and raised the eviction threshold from 0.6 -> 0.75 to reduce churn for short sessions (PR #4121). could be related.

ajay: raising eviction threshold makes reclaim less aggressive -> higher fragmentation if locality is low. if tool loop touches many disjoint keys per iteration, pages won't get reused. can you run with --kv-fingerprint to measure per-page unique-key counts?

maria: ran that quickly. most active pages have unique_keys ~ 300-900 and reuse_count histogram is heavily skewed to 1. many pages only used once then never again, but stay resident.

sam: that suggests poor locality + deferred eviction = high residency. propose two experiments: 1) temporarily revert threshold to 0.6 on canary and enable eager compaction, 2) add per-page reuse_count and distinct-key histogram to the metrics and a paging_latency timer.

chris: also saw kernel-selection branch choosing the "wide-kernel-v2" path for some model shards; that allocates an extra read buffer per page which stays pinned until the streaming chunk completes. combined with deferred eviction this explains the extra ~10-15% memory.

leo: interesting — the batching change reduced small-batch overhead but increased average seq_len and changed chunk boundary alignment. that could worsen page locality.

maria: quick repro command for staging:
```
# run long streaming session with tool loop workload and kv debug flags
cargo run -p runtime --release -- --mode streaming --profile kv --duration 2h \
  --workload tool-loop-heavy --kv-debug --kv-fingerprint --metrics-endpoint http://localhost:9000/metrics
```

maria: attaching pprof link and kv-stats logs to the incident ticket.

infra-bot: deploy d-2026-0315-09 rolled to canary by ajay at 2026-03-15T09:12:00Z

ajay: plan: (A) revert eviction threshold and enable eager compaction on canary for next 6h, (B) add the reuse_count + distinct_keys_per_page histograms to metrics, (C) run the longstream perf test nightly to detect regression. assigning chris + sam to follow up and own metrics. :eyes:

sam: I'll add histograms and a dashboard. will also add an automated assertion to our nightly perf that checks kv_pages_active/resident vs baseline.

chris: I'll instrument kernel-selection path to log when wide-kernel-v2 is picked and correlate with pinned-buffer allocations. also put an opt-in switch to force narrow-kernel for a canary run.

maria: thanks — running revert + eager compaction now, will post updated kv-stats in ~30m.

ajay: once we have updated metrics, let's run a 4h stab with the same tool-loop workload and collect pprof at 5, 60, 180 minutes. we need to prove memory drops between iterations.

maria: noted. will share results.

leo: follow-up hypothesis for root cause: batching heuristic change -> longer average seq -> worse intra-page locality; plus kernel path (`wide-kernel-v2`) pins extra buffers -> prevented eviction -> fragmentation and resident growth on long sessions.

maria: thumbs up, testing now. :thumbsup:

chris: if the revert reduces resident set, we should ship a small fix: either adaptive eviction (based on reuse rate) or per-page lease TTL for pages with low reuse_count. we can A/B test both.

sam: adding it to roadmap. will PR metric names: `kv.page_reuse_count`, `kv.page_distinct_keys`, `kv.eviction_latency_ms`, `kv.fragmentation_pct`.

maria: end-to-end follow-up: gather canary kv-stats + pprofs and then open a postmortem if it regresses in prod. thanks everyone.
